items.title: Ex-Madras HC Justice V Sivagnanam untraceable in Nepal after floods; bar body seeks CJI intervention
items.summary: Former Madras High Court Justice V Sivagnanam has been untraceable in Nepal since flash floods hit the country. The Delhi Tamil Advocates Association has implored Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant to intervene and ask the government authorities to help trace the retired judge and facilitate his safe return to India. In a letter written to the CJI on August 30, the bar body said that while fellow pilgrims were rescued, Justice Sivagnanam could not be reached. He had last contacted his wife on August 26. As per the letter, "The persons travelling in another bus, who were rescued near the APF Nepal Border Outpost at Timure, have informed the family that Justice Sivagnanam’s bus was only about 100–200 metres away from theirs. The family and our Association are, therefore, gravely concerned about his safety and whereabouts." Justice Sivagnanam had a career spanning 34 years in the judiciary. After his retirement, he was designated Senior Advocate by the Supreme Court in July 2025.

items.title: What exactly is PM CARES hiding?
items.summary: Noah saved for the Great Flood. Manu prepared for the deluge. Joseph stored grain for seven years of famine. And then there is our Prime Minister Narendra Modi. By the end of 2024–25, the PM CARES Fund had a closing balance of Rs 8,452 crore. During that financial year, it spent just Rs 87.85 lakh. That’s 0.01 percent spent. So, what exactly is all that money being saved for? A disaster of biblical proportions that perhaps only the PM knows about? Because, honestly, nothing else explains it. If you follow the news, you probably know this by now. After a long delay, the receipts and payments of the PM CARES Fund for 2023–24 and 2024–25 were finally released. And what do they show? That PM CARES spent hardly any money and transferred 93 percent of it into fixed deposits. But the real story of PM CARES is not just that it barely spent money. It is much more dubious. It is about avoiding scrutiny. It is about taking foreign donations. It is about having no stated policy on how much has to be kept in reserves.
